title: Structured-output compatibility probes and auto-revert for staged rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we ship model updates that introduce richer structured output (nested records, optional fields, and typed enums), downstream consumers (console UIs, SDKs, function-call handlers) are exposed to subtle incompatibilities that only show up under realistic traffic patterns. Existing rollout guards cover basic shape diffs but do not: 1) detect enum remapping/semantic changes, 2) measure impact of added optional fields vs. removed required fields, or 3) exercise function-call argument signature evolution across shadow traffic mixes.

Goal: Build a lightweight, extensible compatibility probe layer that runs during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts to: 1) surface semantic diffs (enum/value-level changes), 2) quantify downstream failure/error delta for a candidate variant, and 3) trigger an automated and auditable rollback when defined safety thresholds are exceeded. The system should be low-latency and safe to run in shadow mode (no consumer-side writes).

Scope: runtime-side probe library + control-plane rollout policy hooks + telemetry and dashboarding. This ticket covers the probe definitions, telemetry schema, rollout policy integration, and a first PR to auto-revert a canary when thresholds breach.

Non-goals: full behavioral equivalence testing (heavy fuzzing), deep NLP semantic diffing of freeform text, or rewriting consumer schemas.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compatibility probes run in shadow and canary modes and emit standardized telemetry; 2) The probe detects enum value additions/removals and reports a semantic-delta score; 3) A canary variant crossing the configured severity thresholds causes an auto-revert action that is logged and surfaced in the Console; 4) Dashboard has a time-series comparing baseline vs candidate for: schema errors, function-call mismatches, and consumer-side error rate; 5) Runbook updated with steps to override auto-revert and to opt out for specific models.
tasks: Design probe spec (field-level typing, enum mapping rules, tolerance thresholds)
Implement runtime probe hooks: sample interceptor, signature validator, enum-delta detector
Extend rollout controller with probe-signal integration and auto-revert action
Create telemetry schema and Grafana/Console widgets for comparison views
Author canary experiment: shadow twin + 5% live traffic gating to exercise live downstream SDKs
Write unit+integration tests and a staged rollout PR with feature flag
Update runbook and add a short demo notebook for SREs/PMs
updates: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel - Created ticket: initial problem statement and scope
2026-02-24 Liam O'Connor - Proposed probe spec attached (enum remap, required->optional delta, function-arg signature check). Added tolerance model for optional fields.

2026-03-02 Engineering sync: agreed to implement lightweight scoring (0..1) for semantic delta rather than full semantics. Decided to treat unknown enum values as 'unknown-vote' and surface separately.
2026-03-05 PR opened: runtime probe hooks (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8213). Basic telemetry events emitted: compat.event, compat.score, compat.signature_diff

2026-03-09 Integration test: shadow twin run across internal SDKs revealed a mismatch where new model returns nested 'payment.method' as string vs object expected; probe scored 0.72 and flagged consumer-side failure increase +3.4%.
2026-03-12 Ops review: auto-revert policy v1 approved (score >= 0.6 OR consumer error delta > 2% sustained for 5m triggers revert). Moving ticket to In Review for final sign-off.
review_feedback: Product (Maya Singh): prefer conservative default thresholds; make auto-revert audible in Console with one-click override.
Design (Evan Ruiz): dashboard needs per-route breakdown; add sample payload diffs in the UI panel for quick triage.
Security (Priya Menon): confirm telemetry does not include PII; add redact hooks for sensitive keys in structured payloads.
decision: Implement a probe-first approach: probes run in shadow mode by default, compute a compact compatibility score and a set of signal counts (enum_unknowns, required_missing, shape_mismatch, signature_delta). Rollout controller will evaluate a simple policy expression (score, consumer_error_delta) and perform an automated rollback action that is logged and reversible. Telemetry will be exposed as events and aggregated metrics. We will not attempt deep semantic equivalence in v1.

Run a 48h shadow experiment across 3 downstream SDKs to collect baseline vs candidate signals
